title: Strong reader and writer anchors retain arbitrarily large uncharged allocations
claim: A single real reader or tracked capacity-limited bytes.Buffer can anchor arbitrarily large caller allocations outside the byte budget. GC measurements retained 100663296 bytes with incremental charge 0 for readers and 64 for buffers; untracked controls did not retain them and Finish released them. This explicitly challenges the documented README retained-anchor trade-off under the hard maximum-footprint rule.
repro_command: cd /tmp/ddiast-review/wt/store-memory-bounds && env GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 GOFLAGS=-p=4 DD_IAST_REQUEST_SAMPLING=100 DD_IAST_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=64 DD_IAST_MAX_RANGE_COUNT=64 timeout 900 go test -count=1 -timeout 12m -v -run '^TestBoundsRetainedAnchors$' ./internal/taint/store

title: Non-atomic annotation admission permits unbounded map growth
claim: The capacity check is separated from map insertion, allowing an arbitrary number of simultaneous calls to observe free space and insert independent annotations. A scheduling-only private patch deterministically yielded 2048 live entries against capacity 64, retaining 7651328 extra HeapInuse bytes and zero source charge; the same interleaving reproduced under -race. Request owner permits do not govern AnnotationFor.
repro_command: cd /tmp/ddiast-review/wt/store-memory-bounds && env GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 GOFLAGS=-p=4 DD_IAST_REQUEST_SAMPLING=100 DD_IAST_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=64 DD_IAST_MAX_RANGE_COUNT=64 timeout 900 go test -count=1 -timeout 12m -v -run '^TestBoundsAnnotationAdmission$' ./internal/spans

title: Short evidence parts pin full snapshots outside the event byte budget
claim: Untruncated short value parts retain full sink-snapshot backing, while event admission reserves only new source identity bytes. At supported maximum configuration, real SQL analysis and default redaction/truncation retained an extra 138264576 HeapInuse bytes across 64 events with 64 findings each, 5.49 times the 24 MiB whole-feature ceiling. Each event encoded to 21772 bytes without fallback and exact source identity charge was only 192 bytes process-wide.
